extracted.intended_audience: Depositors of microorganisms, patent applicants and agents, and International Depositary Authorities (IDAs) handling deposits under the Budapest Treaty
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and legal requirements, procedures and quality criteria for making, converting, storing and furnishing deposits of microorganisms with International Depositary Authorities under the Budapest Treaty, including obligations of depositors, patent agents and IDAs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible grounds for IDA refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 6.4(a) specifies the only circumstances in which an IDA may legitimately refuse to accept a microorganism for deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: (i) microorganism is not of a kind the IDA accepts under the Treaty; (ii) the microorganism is so exceptional that the IDA is technically unable to perform required tasks (e.g., a strain too difficult to cultivate); (iii) deposit received in a condition indicating the microorganism is missing or precluding scientific acceptance (e.g., broken receptacle/contamination). Refusal in any other case breaches Treaty obligations and could lead to loss of IDA status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory requirements for acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Rule 6.4(a), the IDA shall accept the microorganism when all the requirements of Rule 6.1(a) or 6.2(a) and Rule 6.3(a) are complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IDA must ensure the depositor has met all mandatory requirements (see paragraphs 11–22). If not complied with, the IDA must immediately notify the depositor in writing and invite compliance. Formal acceptance may be deferred pending compliance, but deferment does not prejudice the date of deposit (except for conversion cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date of deposit (original/new)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the microorganism has been accepted as an original or new deposit, the date of that deposit shall be the date on which the microorganism was received by the international depositary authority (Rule 6.4(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for conversions (Rule 6.4(d)), the physical receipt date is the deposit date even if procedural acceptance requirements are completed later. This date is crucial for patent filing/priority considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of pre-Treaty or non-Budapest deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 6.4(d) permits conversion of a deposit made before an institution became an IDA to be considered a Treaty deposit on the date such status was acquired, provided Rule 6.4(b) requirements are complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion means the deposit's Treaty date becomes the date the collection acquired IDA status (an 'artificial' date). Only the original depositor (or successor in title) may convert. National practices may differ: some offices may treat the physical receipt date as deposit date; others treat the date of request for conversion as the date. Some IDAs may refuse conversion for prior scientific-only deposits because of distribution constraints; in such cases a fresh deposit is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt issuance and mandatory form/content
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving and accepting a microorganism (or conversion), the IDA must notify the depositor by issuing an official receipt on the international form BP/4 (Rule 7.1, Rule 7.2(a),(c) and Rule 7.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receipt must be signed by an authorized representative and contain at least: (i) name/address of IDA; (ii) name/address of depositor; (iii) date of original deposit as per Rule 6.4(c); (iv) depositor's identification reference for the microorganism; (v) accession number assigned by the IDA; (vi) reference to any scientific description/taxonomic designation submitted. The receipt and the first positive viability statement together provide documentary evidence of a Budapest Treaty-compliant deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability testing — timing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The international depositary authority shall test the viability of each microorganism deposited with it promptly after any deposit referred to in Rule 6 or any transfer referred to in Rule 5.1 (Rule 10.1(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 10.1 also requires viability testing at reasonable intervals depending on the kind of microorganism and storage conditions, and at any time on request of the depositor. Frequency is left to the IDA's professional judgment; immediate post-deposit testing is particularly important for establishment of the deposit date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability statement — who and when to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: The international depositary authority shall issue a statement concerning the viability of the deposited microorganism: (i) to the depositor promptly after deposit/transfer; (ii) to the depositor on request at any time; (iii) to any authority/party (other than the depositor) to whom samples were furnished, on request (Rule 10.2(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anyone who has received a sample may request and obtain a viability statement. In cases (ii) and (iii) the statement must refer to the most recent viability tests (Rule 10.2(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the viability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The viability statement shall indicate whether the microorganism is or is no longer viable and shall contain specific identifying information (Rule 10.2(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required contents include: (i) name/address of issuing IDA; (ii) name/address of depositor; (iii) relevant deposit date(s) per Rule 7.3(iii) or most recent deposit/transfer dates; (iv) accession number; (v) date of the test to which the statement refers; (vi) information on test conditions if requested by the recipient and the results were negative. This allows verification of testing in event of negative results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging for viability statements
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDA is entitled to charge for viability statements issued in respect of an original deposit, subject to exceptions (Rules 10.2(e) and 12.1(a)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include the viability statement issued to the depositor immediately after deposit and viability statements issued to industrial property offices; other recipients may be charged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance of initial positive viability statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The first viability statement (post-deposit) is critical because it determines the effective validity of the date of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first viability statement is negative and all subsequent statements are negative, the original date of deposit is lost. If the first statement is positive, it is key to recognition of the original date vis-à-vis any replacement deposit if the microorganism is later lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storage duration and care obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any microorganism deposited with an IDA shall be stored with all care necessary to keep it viable and uncontaminated for at least five years after the most recent request for furnishing a sample and, in any case, for at least 30 years after the date of deposit (Rule 9.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision ensures permanence of deposits and requires IDAs to follow expected culture-collection practices to minimize loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy/confidentiality of deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: No IDA shall give information to anyone whether a microorganism has been deposited under the Treaty, nor give information about any deposited microorganism except to authorities/persons entitled to obtain a sample under Rule 11, and subject to the same conditions (Rule 9.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects secrecy until a related patent application is published. The IDA need not independently ascertain publication status; furnishing is tied to Rule 11 conditions. Some exceptions and practical nuances exist (see paragraphs 92 and 104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Start deposit procedure early
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors should begin the depositing procedure well in advance rather than at the last minute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late deposits risk postal/customs delays, damaged packages, non-viability discovered on testing, or acceptance refusal; these can jeopardize the deposit date and corresponding patent filings. Allow time for unexpected difficulties and for required communications with the IDA and patent agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check shipping/import/quarantine constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: When sending deposits to foreign IDAs, prospective depositors must consider import/quarantine regulations which can cause significant delays or rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some cell lines/viruses may take weeks or months to import. Consult the IDA in advance about acceptance by airmail or necessity for air freight and required shipping documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate packaging and compliance with mail/air freight rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must pack vessels containing microorganisms adequately for transmission per Universal Postal Union and International Air Transport Association regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broken or poorly packed receptacles leading to irrecoverable or contaminated samples will cause IDA refusal (Rule 6.4(a)(iii)). Ensure packaging meets carrier and biosafety rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and correct deposit forms/information
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors should give all the information asked for on the IDA forms, ensure it is correct and expressed in one of the official languages of the IDA (Rule 6.1(a) and paragraph 56 guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms are designed to capture the information required by the Regulations; incomplete or incorrect forms lead to processing delays. Request and follow the IDA's specific administrative and technical requirements (Rule 6.3(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity on identity of depositor and authorized signatory
rubrics_metrics.description: It should be made clear whether the person sending the microorganism is the depositor or acting on behalf of an organization; organization deposits require signature by an authorized official and clarity on notification recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifying this prevents the IDA from withholding information pending verification and ensures official communications go to the intended party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent agent notification/authorization and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent agent will be communicating with the IDA, the depositor should inform the IDA and may request copies of receipt and viability statement to be sent to the agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless instructed otherwise, the IDA communicates only with the depositor. Early briefing of agents and depositors prevents confusion and delay; agents should be briefed on any special handling requirements of the microorganism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity of deposited material
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must meet the IDA requirements regarding the form and quantity of microorganism to be deposited (Rule 6.3(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some IDAs require sufficient material for direct distribution (e.g., cell-lines, plasmids); others prepare their own subcultures for distribution. Meet IDA-specified quantities and formats to avoid rejections or processing issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance submission of information when special arrangements required
rubrics_metrics.description: It is often helpful for an IDA to receive deposit information in advance of the microorganism so arrangements (e.g., special growth medium preparation) can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advance information facilitates prompt handling, but the official date of deposit remains the date of physical receipt. In emergencies prioritize sending the microorganism itself while remembering that without written information the IDA may not be able to test viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity checks of distributed preparations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an IDA distributes its own preparations rather than depositor-supplied material, many IDAs will ask the depositor to check the authenticity of their preparations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not Treaty-mandated, depositors are well-advised to verify authenticity to ensure distributed material corresponds to patent claims and scientific descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion procedural checklist for depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: When converting an existing deposit to a Budapest deposit, the depositor should inform the IDA of the accession number and confirm conversion is permissible, then attend to standard deposit points (administrative/technical requirements, forms, identity, authenticity checks, official communications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conversion is not permitted, a fresh deposit is required. Conversion is important to obtain international recognition (e.g., Japanese Patent Office recognition of non-Budapest deposits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances allowing a new deposit (Article 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 4 allows the depositor, when an IDA cannot furnish samples (e.g., microorganism no longer viable, or export/import restrictions prevent sending samples abroad), to make a new deposit of the originally deposited microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New deposits help preserve availability of the microorganism and protect patent rights; they are subject to conditions and do not apply to microorganisms previously transferred to another IDA unless that IDA is also unable to furnish samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required depositor statement for new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new deposit must be accompanied by a signed statement alleging that the newly deposited microorganism is the same as that originally deposited (Article 4(1)(c); Rule 6.2 summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signed statement must include: (i) required indications under Rule 6.1(a) if new IDA; (ii) reason for new deposit, allegation of identity, and date on which notification of inability to furnish samples was received; (iii) most recent scientific description/taxonomic designation submitted for the previous deposit. The statement must be accompanied by a copy of the previous deposit receipt and the most recent positive viability statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for retaining original deposit date for new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: The new deposit shall be treated as made on the date of the original deposit if all preceding viability statements for the original indicated viability and the new deposit was made within three months after the depositor received notification of the IDA's inability to furnish samples (Article 4(1)(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At least one prior positive viability statement must exist for the original deposit. If these conditions are not met, the earliest date that can be applied to the new deposit is the actual receipt date of the new deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of the three‑month time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods expressed in months are computed per Rule 12bis.2: computation starts the day following the relevant event and expires in the subsequent month on the day with the same number (or the last day if that month lacks the day number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: notification received Jan 15 → new deposit due no later than Apr 15. Notification Jan 31 → new deposit due no later than Apr 30. The three-month limit does not begin until the depositor has received notification, except where IDA has ceased to function or lost status without notifying the depositor; in that case, the limit may start from public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and viability statement content for new deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance of a new deposit the IDA must test viability and issue a receipt (BP/5) and a viability statement; the receipt contains the same basic indications as for an original deposit plus particulars relevant to the new deposit (Rule 7.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to standard receipt items, the new-deposit receipt must indicate (vi) the relevant reason and date given by the depositor under Rule 6.2(a)(ii); (vii) reference to any scientific description/taxonomic designation as applicable; (viii) the accession number given to the previous deposit. If deposited with another IDA, the receipt should give the name and address of the previous IDA. The issuing IDA must also send copies of the receipt and the last positive viability statement issued for the previous deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for timing and risks of new deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositors must ensure a viable sample of the newly deposited microorganism is received by the IDA no later than the last day of the three‑month period to retain the original date; otherwise the earliest applicable date becomes the actual receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New deposits made at the last minute are subject to the same postal, customs, packaging, communication and viability-testing risks as original deposits (see paragraphs 43–49). Prompt action upon receiving IDA notification is essential; note the notification date and calculate the three‑month deadline immediately.
